title: BatchCache Policy Guardrails & Forensic Audit Playbook for Auto-Apply
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Build a security- and compliance-focused playbook and implementation plan for the automatic application and rollback of batching/caching recommendations. The playbook should define RBAC roles, approval flows, immutable audit records, and a minimal safe-set of configuration changes that can be auto-applied. It must integrate with existing change-management workflows, generate forensic-ready logs for regulators, and provide a path for emergency rollback without violating SLOs or security constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Define RBAC roles and permissions required to propose, approve, and execute auto-apply operations
Create a change-management flow that supports canary/small-batch rollout and manual approval gates
All auto-applies emit tamper-evident audit records (who/what/when/why/diff) stored in the compliant audit store
Emergency rollback mechanism that can be triggered automatically by regression detection and manually by SREs
End-to-end integration tests covering role enforcement, audit logging, and rollback scenarios
A short operational runbook and Confluence playbook describing escalation paths and forensic steps
tasks: Inventory auto-applyable config knobs (batch size, KV cache TTL, cache-scope, batching policy) and mark safe/unsafe
Design RBAC model: proposer, approver, operator, auditor roles with least privilege
Prototype audit event schema (immutable events with HMAC/append-only store) and retention policy
Implement change diff capture in the config API and include before/after tokenized snapshots
Wire approvals to existing ticketing flow (link PRD -> Linear ticket -> apply event)
Implement canary rollout controller that applies to a fraction of hosts and monitors cost/latency regressions
Add automated rollback hook tied to regression detector (latency/cost/quality thresholds)
Write E2E tests and a demo script for security review and SOC/A audit team
